Welcome to the Signal Shot community channel.

This is the public home for everyone following or contributing to Signal Shot: BAIF's initiative to bring together AI safety researchers and formal verification experts around a shared moonshot goal: making AI systems verifiable.

A few things to know:

  • #introductions introduce yourself, your background, and what brought you here
  • #beginners no question is too basic; this is a space to learn out loud
  • We'll use this channel to share updates, start technical discussions, and coordinate across teams

Whether you're a formal methods researcher, an AI safety practitioner, a curious newcomer, or somewhere in between - you belong here. The goal is a community that's rigorous and welcoming in equal measure.

Glad you're here!

Hi everyone! :wave:

Sharing two resources from the SVIL2026 public seminar:

:tv: Talk recordings (YouTube playlist): https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLtlBXrgM1AlOg-jxchcgkLfTdwZWm-oN3

:www: Event website: https://beneficial-ai-foundation.github.io/SVIL2026/

A quick note: Derek Sorensen's talk wasn't recorded due to technical difficulties, but his slides are available on the SVIL2026 website above.

Enjoy the talks!

Signal Shot got picked up in two places this month

EvIT (GI / Cyberagentur) ran Bhargavan and Kiefer's write-up on the SPQR work and Runtime Verification published their Rust → Lean pipeline work and mentioned they're planning to take part :point_down:

  • https://www.linkedin.com/posts/signalshot-evit-formalverification-share-7485998906816851968-DnXW/
  • https://trustworthy-it.com/meldungen/detail/formal-analysis-from-design-to-deployment
  • https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/from-rust-code-mathematical-proof-how-we-verify-safety-critical-lzuke/

Worth a look if you haven't seen them. Curious what you all make of it + thoughts and comments are welcome!
